title:
Space engineering
Space segment operability
organisation: ECSS Secretariat, ESA-ESTEC Standards Section (prepared by the ECSS-E-ST-70-11C Rev.1 Working Group)
status_notes: Second issue, Revision 1, dated 15 October 2025, the newest ECSS standard in the library. It revises ECSS-E-ST-70-11C (31 July 2008), which followed ECSS-E-70-11A (5 August 2005); ECSS-E-70-11B was never issued (change log, p. 3). The change log notes that a new DOORS module, not linked to the previous version, was created because of the number of changes.

contents.title: Terms specific to the present standard
Autonomy for execution of nominal mission operations
The ECSS-E-ST-70-41 Telemetry and telecommand packet utilization standard

key_points.text: Rev.1 aligns the scope of ECSS-E-ST-70-11 with ECSS-E-ST-70-41 to avoid overlap, rewrites clause 5.8 as complementary PUS operability requirements, updates the Annex A mission constants and removes the former Annex B tailoring guide.
Six operability categories are defined: commandability, compatibility, deactivation, flexibility, observability and testability.

An essential telecommand is distributed without on-board software; a high priority command is a pulse command routed to hardware by a CPDU; high priority telemetry reports mission-critical equipment status under all circumstances.
Mission-dependent quantities are 'mission constants' written in angle brackets, e.g. <TC_VERIF_DELAY>, and summarised in Annex A.
No telecommand executed at the wrong time or configuration may lead to loss of the mission; mission-critical functions can be protected with two independent telecommands (e.g. ARM and FIRE).
Security: implementing CCSDS 355.0-B SDLS (Baseline Mode for TC Authentication) and CCSDS 355.1-B Extended Procedures is recommended.
Different data classes get different downlink bandwidth through physical and virtual channels; the VC-to-data-class assignment does not change during the mission, but the bandwidth allocation can.
Telemetered values must be self-contained (no delta or change-only telemetry), and fast-changing critical parameters such as pyro currents must be latched and the latched value telemetered.

A telemetry parameter keeps the same structure and interpretation in every packet; super-commutated parameters are sampled regularly; housekeeping packets do not use sub-commutation; packets of one APID on one VC are delivered in generation order.

Idle frames go on a dedicated virtual channel; idle packets only complete a frame that already holds a meaningful packet; all packets except idle, time and HPTM packets are available for on-board storage.
On-board time must be settable by TC, monotonically increasing in all modes and never wrap around; all telemetry source packets should carry an on-board generation time in their header.

The sampling time of a parameter in a non-variable packet must be derivable from the packet generation time by an implicitly known offset; GNSS-based OBT must report the GNSS/OBT correlation and handle leap seconds autonomously.
A telecommand contains one and only one on-board function, keeps the same action definition for the whole mission (no flip/flop commands) and must not cause permanent loss of commanding.
With COP-1 and the AD service, the sliding window must be configured for in-orbit conditions so as not to limit the uplink rate artificially.
Mission-critical functions need at least two separate command actions (arm/enable then execute); critical register loads need a separate execute command.

Every TC except pure hardware (CPDU) commands gets acceptance-stage verification; invalid TCs (wrong length, CRC or APID) fail at acceptance; success reports can be disabled; register loads are echoed by dedicated telemetry parameters.
Autonomy levels: E1 (ground control) to E4 (goal-oriented on-board re-planning) for mission execution, and D1 (essential data storage) to D2 (all mission data) for data management.

PUS operability: one or more application processes per subsystem; APID assignment fixed for the mission; APID + type + subtype (plus further fields) uniquely identify packet structure; HK packets have fixed content and fixed sample-time offsets; parameter IDs are unique across the spacecraft.
Time-tagged TCs with equal release times are not rejected but released one after the other; TCs that 'elapsed' while a schedule was disabled are not released when it is re-enabled.
A mission must be able to define maximum TC and TM packet lengths below the CCSDS maxima, and must support large-packet uplink and downlink by splitting.

TT&C: at least two receivers on different antennas are always active; TCs with repetitive bit patterns must be processed without error (CCSDS 231.0-B randomisation is suggested); a ground-configurable <NO_TC_TIMEOUT> triggers on-board contingency recovery.
Annex A defines 23 mission constants, e.g. <TIME_CORREL_ACCUR>, <TC_VERIF_DELAY>, <SAFE_TIME>, <NO_TC_TIMEOUT>, <MIN_DATA_RATE_SM> and <CEL_DUMP_TIME>.

notes: Printed page numbers equal PDF page numbers, and PDF page 85 is blank (the registry gives 84 pages). Requirement identifiers run from ECSS-E-ST-70-11_1670001 upwards (e.g. _1670399 on p. 81). The change log uses the short forms 'ECSS-E-70-11C' and 'ECSS-E-70-41C' and has the typo 'standardarised' (p. 3). Definition 3.2.3.35 refers to 'ECSS-S-ST-70-41', an apparent typo for ECSS-E-ST-70-41 (p. 15). The normative references cite the adoption notices and CCSDS books without issue numbers (p. 9). Requirement 5.5.1t prints 'ECSS-E-AS-50-26and' (p. 38). The bibliography is short and omits several standards cited in the text, such as CCSDS 232.0-B and 231.0-B (pp. 63, 71).
